scaling_probe.configuration: rustc -O, edition2024, no features; only each measurement process pinned to lowest allowed logical CPU (affinity mask0x1); clocks/priority not fixed; before then after,8warmups and9samples per scenario
scaling_probe.measured_scope: Public Graph::compile consumes a prebuilt declaration graph; explicit dependency timing excludes pool and pass preparation. Preparation, Graph input build and plan destruction are outside these timing windows. Full lifecycle allocation gates are separate.
scaling_probe.patterns: One buffer; N independent writes, ascending/descending/fixed-seed shuffled offsets. Gapped writes have4-byte payload and4-byte holes, all passes side effects. Wide-read case uses adjacent4-byte writes then one whole-buffer read. Dependency case constructs N empty declaration passes then N-1 chain edges.

first_unpinned_run.note: Preserved initial8warmup/9sample run. Unpinned timings varied; contributions from scheduling, clocks and background work were not isolated. The same process affinity was added to both measurement executables, not to the Renderer.

reproduction: Write harness_source_utf8 to scaling.rs; create a detached baseline checkout at baseline_commit with Git LFS smudge disabled.
Run scaling-before.exe then scaling-after.exe, separately from builds and GPU gates; keep all raw samples.
limits: Synthetic CPU workload; no GPU, displayed FPS or full application speedup claim.
Ascending array-friendly compile and broad-read ascending inputs get slower; record both directions.
No fixed wall-clock threshold in CI. AVL metadata and updates cost more than the favorable old array case.
